title: Purple Sector: choose the redesign direction
question: Each card shows the Feed screen on a phone. Open a card's expand chip for the full sketch. Keep the lead direction, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Trackside
options.lineage: Circuit signage: corner-number boards, 300/200/100 braking boards, kerbs
options.thesis: The app reads like the signs at the edge of a circuit: big black numbers on white boards, readable at speed.
materials: white sign boards on concrete grey
options.viewport: Feed: a white home-course board with a huge time, lap cards as numbered boards, kerb stripe under the active tab.
options.risk: A light ground is a big change from the current dark app; night drives need a dark HUD variant.

raised.raise: Sector results also differ in form: purple is a doubled kerb, green solid, yellow dashed, so colour is never the only signal.
A finished lap gets the whole first screen; the next lap is one swipe away.
Every lap of a route is drawn at the same scale and orientation, so shapes line up when compared.
One column grid for every time: decimals line up across the feed, leaderboards and the HUD.
Blue appears only on things you can press.

options.label: Livery
options.lineage: Race-car paint schemes and race-number roundels
options.thesis: The app is painted like a race car: white body, navy panels, and a purple-green-yellow stripe that is the brand.
options.viewport: Feed: navy header panel cut by the tri-stripe, each driver shown as a race-number roundel, lap cards on white.
options.risk: The most familiar choice: racing stripes are where most motorsport apps land.

options.label: Paddock Pass
options.lineage: Boarding passes and live departure boards
options.thesis: Every lap is a ticket torn into segments, and leaderboards re-rank in place like a gate board.
materials: rows that slide when the ranking changes
options.viewport: Feed: laps as passes (route, time, sectors, date) on a graphite ground; a new personal best stays lit until seen.
options.case: Fuses well: laps map to passes and rankings to the board. Strong on clarity, weaker on whether drivers see themselves in it.
options.risk: Reads as a travel app if the motorsport colour rules are not held tightly.

options.label: Emission Rail
options.thesis: State shown by line height, dash and doubling instead of colour.
options.viewport: Every screen hangs off one rail of hairline ticks.
options.case: Hairlines vanish in sunlight in a mounted phone.
options.kept: Sector state is also shown by form, not only colour.

options.label: Vertical Feed
options.thesis: One lap owns the whole screen, the next is one flick away.
options.viewport: A full-screen posted lap with actions down the right.
options.case: Laps are numbers and maps, not video; browsing many laps gets slower.
options.kept: A finished lap gets the whole first screen.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: Every plate at one scale so change reads directly.
options.viewport: Laps as engraved plates in a row.
options.case: Drivers do not identify with botany; cream and serif is a default look.
options.kept: All laps of a route drawn at the same scale and orientation.

options.label: Grid Specimen
options.lineage: Wim Crouwel grid posters (shown in the last round)
options.thesis: Times built cell by cell on a visible grid.
options.viewport: Feed set on a visible construction grid.
options.case: Already offered last round and not chosen.
options.kept: One column grid aligns every time on every screen.

options.label: Warm Consumer App
options.thesis: Soft cards, warm ground, one colour for anything pressable.
options.viewport: A column of soft cards over a bottom bar.
options.case: Generic; nothing says motorsport or timing.
options.kept: The action colour appears only on things you can press.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A sports-tracker app done cleanly: white feed cards, map thumbnails, one orange action colour.
canonCard.viewport: Feed of posted laps as activity cards with a map thumbnail and kudos row.
canonCard.risk: Looks like every fitness tracker; Purple Sector loses its own identity.
